incidents.name: Multiple US endpoints experiencing timeouts and latency

content.text: Description of the Issue:

A MongoDB database that stores data for our Agents Platform became unresponsive in our US cluster following a database maintenance operation. This slowed down or blocked many requests, and during the incident roughly 45% of US calls failed and 7% of API requests returned errors.
Root Cause

The unresponsiveness was triggered by a background database maintenance operation (MongoDB expected to provide detailed response as routine operation should not lead to interruption). The database’s built-in protections kicked in as designed, but they stalled writes instead of recovering on their own, and the failure repeated each time we switched to a healthy server.
Fixes only held briefly because the underlying pressure remained. We worked with our database vendor, MongoDB, to stabilise the cluster, and added capacity to bring it back to full health.
Preventative Actions & Learnings:
Retrospective with MongoDB team on resilient changes required on configuration
Coordination with MongoDB on how background database operations are scheduled and approved.
Additional alerting on database health indicators (queue depth, cache pressure, connection counts) that showed strain before users see errors
We’re moving data that Agents Platform calls depend on onto a dedicated, smaller cluster, so it’s less exposed to load elsewhere.
Multi-region resilience. We’re replicating this cluster across multiple US regions, reducing the chance that a single region or server failure causes downtime.
Timeline:
08:50: Impact began.
08:54: An automated alert fired for a high ElevenAgents API error rate, and the on-call team began investigating.
09:10: Database query timeouts were identified, pointing to a database-side issue.
09:21: A support case was opened with MongoDB.
09:25: An overloaded database server that was stalling writes was identified.
09:32: Service briefly recovered, then failed again at 09:46.
09:59 A working call began with MongoDB engineers.
10:15 Traffic was manually switched to a healthy database server, and service briefly recovered at 10:19.
10:43 Failures returned, and the original server was still unable to recover.
11:06: Background shard rebalancing was paused to reduce load.
12:08: Service briefly recovered after MongoDB manually brought the original server back online.
12:26: Failures returned.
12:27: A capacity upgrade was started.
12:45: The upgrade was delayed by cloud provider capacity limits in the region, and MongoDB began manually restarting and repairing the stuck servers.
13:14: Service fully recovered.
14:18: The remaining servers were upgraded one at a time, with traffic first moved to a healthy server.
14:34: All servers were back online.

**Description of the Issue:
**A MongoDB database that stores data for our Agents Platform became unresponsive in our US cluster following a database maintenance operation. This slowed down or blocked many requests, and during the incident roughly 45% of US calls failed and 7% of API requests returned errors.

 

**Root Cause**

The unresponsiveness was triggered by a background database maintenance operation (MongoDB expected to provide detailed response as routine operation should not lead to interruption). The database’s built-in protections kicked in as designed, but they stalled writes instead of recovering on their own, and the failure repeated each time we switched to a healthy server.

Fixes only held briefly because the underlying pressure remained. We worked with our database vendor, MongoDB, to stabilise the cluster, and added capacity to bring it back to full health.

 

**Preventative Actions & Learnings:**

• Retrospective with MongoDB team on resilient changes required on configuration

• Coordination with MongoDB on how background database operations are scheduled and approved.

• Additional alerting on database health indicators (queue depth, cache pressure, connection counts) that showed strain before users see errors

• We’re moving data that Agents Platform calls depend on onto a dedicated, smaller cluster, so it’s less exposed to load elsewhere.

• Multi-region resilience. We’re replicating this cluster across multiple US regions, reducing the chance that a single region or server failure causes downtime.

   

**Timeline:**

• 08:50: Impact began.

• 08:54: An automated alert fired for a high ElevenAgents API error rate, and the on-call team began investigating.

incidents.name: Agents, STT, and Creative Platform: Increased Latency, Conversation Failures, and STT Failures

content.text: Root Cause Analysis: Increased Latency and Failures Across Agents, Speech to Text, and Creative Platform
Duration:
September 29, 2026, 15:56 UTC to 19:36 UTC
Description of the Issue:
Customers experienced increased latency and failed requests on ElevenAgents conversations, Speech to Text, and Creative Platform products, including Sound Effects.
Root Cause:

Processing a request included recording and storing its usage metrics. Under peak traffic the internal usage datastore became overloaded and stopped accepting new connections. Because requests waited on this step to complete, the slowdown affected every product that records usage in it.
Timeline & Actions Taken:
Latency and error rates begin rising across affected products.
Alert fires; engineering begins investigating.
Issue localized to the internal usage datastore.
Incident declared as impact on Agents and Speech to Text is confirmed.
Usage metric datastore recovers; error rates return to baseline.
Full recovery confirmed across all affected products.
Preventative Actions & Learnings:
Decoupling usage recording from request processing, so the usage metric datastore can no longer affect request latency or availability.

write_up_contents.markdown:
# Root Cause Analysis: Increased Latency and Failures Across Agents, Speech to Text, and Creative Platform

## **Duration:** 

September 29, 2026, 15:56 UTC to 19:36 UTC

## **Description of the Issue:** 

Customers experienced increased latency and failed requests on ElevenAgents conversations, Speech to Text, and Creative Platform products, including Sound Effects.

## **Root Cause:** 

Processing a request included recording and storing its usage metrics. Under peak traffic the internal usage datastore became overloaded and stopped accepting new connections. Because requests waited on this step to complete, the slowdown affected every product that records usage in it.

## **Timeline & Actions Taken:**

**15:56 UTC:** Latency and error rates begin rising across affected products.

**16:34 UTC:** Alert fires; engineering begins investigating.

**17:32 UTC:** Issue localized to the internal usage datastore.

**18:26 UTC:** Incident declared as impact on Agents and Speech to Text is confirmed.

**19:36 UTC:** Usage metric datastore recovers; error rates return to baseline.

**20:23 UTC:** Full recovery confirmed across all affected products.

## Preventative Actions & Learnings:

Decoupling usage recording from request processing, so the usage metric datastore can no longer affect request latency or availability.
